citations.quote:
Fix a root degree $\alpha$ of height $r$. Assume integral balancedness and global lifts in every degree of height $<r$ for both the negative half and all dominant highest modules, including based-quotient compatibility there and the negative-half string-ideal membership of each lower lift $G_\infty(b)$ whenever $b\in\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B_\infty$. Then for every $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$:

(i) the image string ideal $J_{(i,n)}^A$ in each highest module $V(\lambda)$, with its rational zero- and infinity-chart intersections, is integrally balanced in degree $\lambda-\alpha$, and its balanced $\mathbb Z$-intersection maps isomorphically to the $\mathbb Z$-span of $\mathcal B_\lambda\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B_\lambda$ in that degree;

(ii) the half ideal $I_{(i,n)}^A$ is integrally balanced in degree $-\alpha$, with balanced intersection mapping isomorphically to the $\mathbb Z$-span of $\mathcal B_\infty\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B_\infty$; and

(iii) their Laurent extensions are free $A$-modules with the adapted global lifts.

Freeness, the chart intersections and the eventual module saturation $J_{(i,n)}^A=V_A(\lambda)\cap F_i^nV(\lambda)$ are conclusions, not hypotheses.

Let $V$ be finite-dimensional over $\mathbb Q(q)$, let $M\subset V$ be an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-submodule spanning $V$, and let $L_0,L_\infty$ be full free $A_0$- and $A_\infty$-lattices in $V$. Write $E=M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$ and use the balanced-triple language of [[def-balanced-triple-and-globalization-map]].

(1) If the canonical $\mathbb Z$-linear map $E\to(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$ is an isomorphism, then
$$M\cap L_0\cong\mathbb Z[q]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E,\qquad M\cap L_\infty\cong\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E,\qquad M\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E,$$
and the infinity residue map $E\to(M\cap L_\infty)/(M\cap q^{-1}L_\infty)$ is also an isomorphism; moreover $A_0\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E\cong L_0$ and $A_\infty\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E\cong L_\infty$ under the maps induced by inclusions. If $E$ has a finite $\mathbb Z$-basis, these are actual free bases of $M,L_0,L_\infty$ over $A,A_0,A_\infty$. No containment $M\subset L_0\cap L_\infty$ and no freeness of $M/E$ is assumed.

(2) If a $\mathbb Z$-module $F$ maps into $M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$, generates $M$ over $A$, and maps injectively into both rational residues $L_0/qL_0$ and $L_\infty/q^{-1}L_\infty$, then $F\cong E\cong(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$.

(3) More generally, let $N\subset M$ be an $A$-submodule whose integral intersection $E_N=N\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$ satisfies $N\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_N$. If a $\mathbb Z$-module $F$ maps to $M\cap(L_0+N)\cap(L_\infty+N)$, generates $M$ modulo $N$ over $A$, and maps injectively into $(L_0+\mathbb QN)/(qL_0+\mathbb QN)$ and $(L_\infty+\mathbb QN)/(q^{-1}L_\infty+\mathbb QN)$, then $M$ is balanced. The sequence
$$0\to(N\cap L_0)/(N\cap qL_0)\to(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)\to(L_0+\mathbb QN)/(qL_0+\mathbb QN)$$
is exact, and its last image is the image of $F$. If $F$ and $E_N$ are finite free $\mathbb Z$-modules, then so is $E_M=M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$, and $M$ is free over $A$.

These are the integral forms of Kashiwara's chart lemmas, in the notation of [[def-balanced-triple-and-globalization-map]]; their rational base extension gives the usual $A_0/A_\infty$ criterion, and no containment of charts or freeness of $M$ is assumed anywhere.

Let $i\in I$ and let $e_i'$ be the skew derivation of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], with string decomposition $u=\sum_lF_i^{(l)}u_l$, $u_l\in\ker e_i'$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]).

(i) If $u\in U_A^-$ then all $u_l$ lie in $U_A^-$. The integral projector is
$$P_i=\sum_l(-1)^lq_i^{-l(l-1)/2}F_i^{(l)}(e_i')^l,\qquad u_l=q_i^{l(l-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^lu,$$
where all powers of $e_i'$ are ordinary powers, not divided by $[l]_i!$.

(ii) Define
$$I_{(i,n)}^A:=U_A^-\cap F_i^nU_q^-=\bigoplus_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}\bigl(\ker e_i'\cap U_A^-\bigr)=\sum_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}U_A^-,$$
$$J_{(i,n)}^A:=\pi_\lambda\bigl(I_{(i,n)}^A\bigr)=\sum_{l\ge n}F_i^{(l)}V_A(\lambda),$$
with $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$ and $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$ as in [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]]. The latter is an $A$-submodule inside the field string-image subspace $F_i^nV(\lambda)$, not a $U_q$-submodule or a $U_A$-stable lattice in general; its equality with $V_A(\lambda)\cap F_i^nV(\lambda)$ is proved after the adapted global basis construction, not presumed here.

(iii) The integral residue of $I_{(i,n)}^A\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$ is the free $\mathbb Z$-span of $\mathcal B(\infty)\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B(\infty)$, and the corresponding rational residue of $F_i^nU_q^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$ is its $\mathbb Q$-span. Integral balancedness of the zero/infinity triple of $I_{(i,n)}^A$ is a conclusion of the subsequent string-ideal induction, not an input.

(iv) On every $U_A$-stable integrable module lattice $M_A$, if a label $\mu$ satisfies $\langle h_i,\mu\rangle=-n\le-1$, then every $u\in(M_A)_\mu$ satisfies the finite identity
$$u=\sum_{k\ge n}(-1)^{k-n}\binom{k-1}{k-n}_iF_i^{(k)}E_i^{(k)}u,$$
and consequently $(M_A)_\mu=\sum_{k\ge n}F_i^{(k)}(M_A)_{\mu+k\alpha_i}$. This is the exact boundary generation supplier used in the string-ideal induction.

Let $\star$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear anti-involution of $U_q^-$ fixing each generator $F_i$, so that for a word $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_r}$ one has $(F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_r})^\star=F_{i_r}\cdots F_{i_1}$, and let $B$ be the normalized Kashiwara half form of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]]. Then $\star$ is a well-defined anti-involution of the Serre quotient, reverses negative words, preserves the divided-power integral form $U_A^-$ of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], commutes with the bar involution $\psi$, and preserves $B$: $B(P^\star,Q^\star)=B(P,Q)$. Consequently $\star$ preserves the crystal lattice $\mathcal L(\infty)$ of [[lem-crystal-lattice-polarizations-are-perfect-at-q-zero]], the integral residue lattice $L_{\mathbb Z}(\infty)=U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$, and the bar lattice $L_{\mathbb Z}^-=U_A^-\cap\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$ of [[lem-integral-crystal-residues-of-the-negative-half-represent-the-crystal-basis]]. On the integral crystal residue the induced map permutes $\mathcal B(\infty)\cup(-\mathcal B(\infty))$. Only this signed lattice preservation is asserted, not an unsigned $\star$-crystal theorem; the sign is what the gluing of the string-ideal global lifts requires.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]). Let $\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda),\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$ be the lattices and generating residue sets of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], let $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ be the Kashiwara operators, let $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$, and let $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu},\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}$ be the tensor maps of [[lem-highest-weight-tensor-maps-and-their-adjunction]]. For $\alpha=\sum_in_i\alpha_i\in Q_+$ write $|\alpha|:=\sum_in_i$ and $Q_+(r):=\{\alpha\in Q_+:\ |\alpha|\le r\}$.

(i) For every integer $r\ge0$ the following interlocking statements are all true.

- A(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ for all $i\in I$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- B(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ for all $i$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- C(r): for all $i$, $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $b\in\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}$ and $b'\in\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, one has $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$.
- D(r): for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}/q\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.
- E(r): for all $\lambda,\mu\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\Phi_{\lambda,\mu}(\mathcal L(\lambda+\mu)_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha})\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal L(\mu)$.
- F(r): for all $\lambda,\mu\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}((\mathcal L(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal L(\mu))_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha})\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda+\mu)$.
- G(r): $\Psi_{\lambda,\mu}((\mathcal B(\lambda)\otimes\mathcal B(\mu))_{\lambda+\mu-\alpha})\subseteq\mathcal B(\lambda+\mu)\cup\{0\}$ for all $\lambda,\mu$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- H(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$ for all $i$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- I(r): $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$ for all $i$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- J(r): for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$ and $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\tilde e_ib\neq0$, one has $b=\tilde f_i\tilde e_ib$.
- K(r): $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}/q\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- L(r): $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ for all $\lambda\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$.
- M(r): for all $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $i\in I$, $\lambda\in P^+$ and $P\in\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, one has $\tilde f_i(Pv_\lambda)\equiv(\tilde f_iP)v_\lambda\bmod q\mathcal L(\lambda)$.
- N(r): for all $\lambda\in P^+$ and $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$, $\pi_\lambda$ induces a bijection $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.
- O(r): for all $\lambda\in P^+$, $\alpha\in Q_+(r)$ and $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0$, one has $\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)=\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)$.

(ii) Consequently $(\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda))$ is a crystal basis of $V(\lambda)$ in the sense of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]: $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ is a crystal lattice of $V(\lambda)$, $\mathcal B(\lambda)$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda)$ with $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$, the operators satisfy $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ and the partial-inverse axiom, and $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}V(\lambda)_\mu=\#\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ for all $\mu$. The lattices $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ are free $A_0$-modules.

Let $\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq U_q^-$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ be the Kashiwara lattice and generating set of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], with the Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]](iii).

(i) $(\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty))$ is a crystal basis of $U_q^-$ in the sense of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]: $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is a free $A_0$-submodule with $U_q^-\cong\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{A_0}\mathcal L(\infty)$, stable under $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$; and $\mathcal B(\infty)$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ satisfying $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$, $\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)$, and $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$ for all $b,b'\in\mathcal B(\infty)$.

(ii) The root-graded components are free: $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ is a free $A_0$-module of rank $\#\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}=\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}U_q^-[-\nu]$.

(iii) For every $\lambda\in P^+$ the projection $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$ maps $\mathcal B(\infty)$ onto $\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$, and the compatibility statements of [[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]] hold: $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\cong\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, $\tilde f_i\pi_\lambda=\pi_\lambda\tilde f_i$ and $\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)=\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)$ whenever $\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0$.

(iv) The root-graded crystal has finite $\varepsilon_i$ on each element, formal $\varphi_i=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$, and actual lowering length $\ell_i^-=\infty$. Every $\tilde f_i$-iterate is nonzero because $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ holds on its lattice and residue. Thus it is the infinite lowering crystal of the unit, with the negative-half convention of the crystal-graph definition.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and enters only through the grand loop: the partial-inverse axiom in (i) uses clause J(r) of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]], whose proof consumes the AC-dependent form comparison of the negative-half form. The freeness and rank statements are choice-free.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $\mathcal L(\lambda),\mathcal B(\lambda),\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$ be the lattices and bases of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $P\mapsto Pv_\lambda$, and Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$. Then for every $\alpha\in Q_+$, every $i\in I$ and every $\lambda\in P^+$:

(a) **Lattice projection.** $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.

(b) **Operator compatibility modulo $q$.** For every $P\in\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, $\tilde f_i(Pv_\lambda)\equiv(\tilde f_iP)v_\lambda\bmod q\mathcal L(\lambda)$, and for every $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ with $\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0$, $\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)=\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)$ in $\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda)$. Equivalently $\tilde f_i\pi_\lambda=\pi_\lambda\tilde f_i$ on $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$, where the left-hand side is computed in $V(\lambda)$.

(c) **Basis projection.** The map induced by $\pi_\lambda$ is a bijection $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$.

(d) **Large-weight form.** If all $\lambda(h_j)$, $j\in I$, are sufficiently large compared with $\alpha$, then $\pi_\lambda$ induces isomorphisms $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, and the congruences of (b) for such $\lambda$ are the computation used inside the grand loop to deduce the general case; the general statements (a)-(c) hold for every $\lambda\in P^+$, without a largeness hypothesis.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: clause (c) is clause N(r) of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]], whose proof applies clause J(r), and J(r) is where the AC-dependent form comparison of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] is used. Clauses (a), (b) and (d) are themselves choice-free.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]); in this page we write $V(\lambda):=L(\lambda)$, following the notation of the crystal sources. Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), and let $A_0$ be the crystal limiting ring ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]).

Define $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $V(\lambda)$ generated by all vectors $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda$ ($r\ge0$, $i_1,\dots,i_r\in I$), where for $r=0$ the vector is $v_\lambda$; and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $U_q^-$ generated by all $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ ($r\ge0$), where $\mathbf 1$ is the unit of $U_q^-$. Here $\tilde f_i$ on $V(\lambda)$ are the module Kashiwara operators and $\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ are the negative-half operators. Define
$$\mathcal B(\lambda):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda+q\mathcal L(\lambda):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda),$$
$$\mathcal B(\infty):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1+q\mathcal L(\infty):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty).$$

Then, with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$:

(a) $\mathcal L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ with $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu=\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap V(\lambda)_\mu$, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ with $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}=\mathcal L(\infty)\cap U_q^-[-\nu]$; correspondingly $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)=\bigsqcup_\nu\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}$.

(b) $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ and $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$.

(c) (Recursive spanning.) For $\alpha\in Q_+\setminus\{0\}$,
$$\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad \mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}\Bigr)\setminus\{0\},$$
and the same formulas with $\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$. Each $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is generated over $A_0$ by finitely many monomials of total length at most $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$, hence is a finitely generated $A_0$-module.

No basis property, scalar-extension spanning or crystal-lattice property of $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ or $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is asserted here; these are conclusions of the grand loop. The script letters avoid the collision with the simple module $L(\lambda)$. No choice principle is used. Each fixed component is torsionfree inside a field vector space and generated by finitely many words of its fixed height, so it is free over the DVR $A_0$; its full field-span is proved later. The field map $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective, but exact equality on Kashiwara monomial generators is not asserted.

Let $L_{\mathbb Z}(\infty)=U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$ be the integral residue lattice of [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]], with $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}\to\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ the canonical injection. Then the image of this injection is exactly $\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)}\mathbb Z b$; in particular $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$ is a free $\mathbb Z$-module with basis $\mathcal B(\infty)$, and after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$ it is the full rational crystal space $\mathbb Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\bigoplus_b\mathbb Zb=\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$.

The normalized Kashiwara half form of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] takes values on $U_A^-$ in $K_{\mathbb Z}=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1},(1-q^{2n})^{-1}:n\ge1]$ and on $L_{\mathbb Z}$ in $A_{\mathbb Z}=\mathbb Z[q,(1-q^{2n})^{-1}:n\ge1]$; consequently its residue pairing on $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$ is $\mathbb Z$-valued. In the residue basis $\mathcal B(\infty)$ the coefficients of an integral element are its integer pairings with the basis vectors, and the norm-$1$ elements of the integral residue $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$ are exactly $\mathcal B(\infty)\cup(-\mathcal B(\infty))$. The Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ preserve $L_{\mathbb Z}$, hence induce endomorphisms of the integral residue subgroup. No $A$-module structure on $L_{\mathbb Z}$, no identification of the integral residue with the rational residue as a $\mathbb Z$-module, and no unsigned norm-$1$ characterization is asserted; the module integral residue basis is established only in the globalization theorem of this page.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let $M$ be a
$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module
([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) whose support is contained in
a finite union of cones,

$$\operatorname{supp}M\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^{s}(\lambda_j-Q_+)\qquad(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_s\in P),$$

where $Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$. Choose a finite free direct
coordinate summand $X_f\subseteq P$ (with respect to a free basis of $P$,
[[def-free-abelian-group]]) containing all $\lambda_j$ and all $\alpha_i$, and
set

$$Y_{\mathrm{aux}}:=\Bigl(\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb ZH_i\Bigr)\oplus\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z),\qquad X_{\mathrm{aux}}:=\operatorname{Hom}(Y_{\mathrm{aux}},\mathbb Z),$$

with the evaluation pairing $X_{\mathrm{aux}}\times Y_{\mathrm{aux}}\to\mathbb Z$.
Define $j\colon X_f\to X_{\mathrm{aux}}$ by $j(x)(H_i):=\langle x,h_i\rangle$ and
$j(x)(f):=f(x)$ for $f\in\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z)$, and put
$\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}:=j(\alpha_i)$. Then:

(i) $(I,A,D,X_{\mathrm{aux}},Y_{\mathrm{aux}},q)$ with the simple roots
$\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$ and simple coroots $H_i$ is a symmetrizable Cartan
datum for a quantum group with the same generalized Cartan matrix $A$ and the
same symmetrizer $D$; its pairing is perfect, the $\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$ are
linearly independent, the $H_i$ are primitive and independent, and integral
fundamental weights $\Lambda_j$ ($\Lambda_j(H_i)=\delta_{ij}$) exist. Here
$\langle\alpha_j^{\mathrm{aux}},H_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ is the original convention
([[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]],
[[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]]).

(ii) $M$ carries a unique structure of $X_{\mathrm{aux}}$-graded type-one
quantum weight module for the auxiliary datum with
$\operatorname{supp}M^{\mathrm{aux}}\subseteq j(X_f)$, namely
$$M^{\mathrm{aux}}_{j(x)}:=M_x\quad(x\in X_f),\qquad M^{\mathrm{aux}}_{\xi}:=0\quad(\xi\notin j(X_f)),$$
$$K_{(n,f)}\ \text{acts on}\ M_x\ \text{by}\ q^{\sum_in_i\langle x,h_i\rangle+f(x)}\qquad\bigl((n,f)\in\textstyle\bigoplus_i\mathbb ZH_i\oplus\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z)\bigr),$$
with the actions of $E_i$, $F_i$ and of the simple coroots
$K_{d_iH_i}$ unchanged. In particular the old $K_h$ action is recovered from
the label $x$ as $q^{\langle x,h\rangle}$, and the old and auxiliary $E_i,F_i$
actions agree.

(iii) The two recipes are inverse on objects and grading-preserving morphisms:
on $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-modules with labels in $X_f$ and support as above, the
identity on underlying vector spaces is an equivalence between the category of
$P$-graded type-one modules and the corresponding full subcategory of
$X_{\mathrm{aux}}$-graded type-one modules with labels in $j(X_f)$. This is not
an embedding of the old torus algebra into the new one and is asserted only
inside this finite-support category.

(iv) The construction applies simultaneously to Verma modules and highest weight
modules (supported in $\lambda-Q_+$) and to finite tensor products of such
modules (labels add), by choosing one $X_f$ containing all participating upper
weights and all simple roots; the tensor-product $E_i,F_i$ formulas of [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]] are unchanged because only the diagonal toral characters change.

(v) Rationally, $h_{\mathrm{aux}}:=Y_{\mathrm{aux}}\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$
decomposes as $h_{\mathrm{aux}}=H_{\min}\oplus Z$, where $H_{\min}$ is a
minimal realization of $A$ (of dimension $2n-r$, $n=|I|$, $r=\operatorname{rank}A$)
and $Z\subseteq\ker\alpha$ is a complement on which all $\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$
vanish, so the elements of $Z$ are central in the correspondingly extended
Kac–Moody algebra; hence the classical Cartan and multiplicity comparisons of
[[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]] apply to
$H_{\min}$.

Let $\lambda\in P$ be a dominant integral label weight, put
$m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the quantum Verma
module with highest vector $v_\lambda$
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]],
[[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

(i) The quotient $\tilde L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$
is nonzero, has finite-dimensional label weights and support contained in
$\lambda-Q_+$, is integrable, and equals the canonical simple highest weight
module $L(\lambda)$, which is simple also as an ordinary (not assumed graded)
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module.

(ii) **Universality.** Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of
highest weight $\lambda$ with highest vector $v\ne0$ receives a
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module map $\tilde L(\lambda)\to V$ with
$\bar v_\lambda\mapsto v$, and this map is unique; every nonzero such $V$ is
isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$.

(iii) Its character equals the classical integrable highest weight character of
the explicitly regularized realization of the datum. No global
$\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness and no crystal or global basis is used.

Let $\lambda\in P$ be dominant integral, so $m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$
for all $i$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the Verma module with highest vector
$v_\lambda$ ([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]]).
Put $s_i:=F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$.

(i) Every $s_i$ is a singular (highest weight) vector of weight
$\lambda-(m_i+1)\alpha_i$.

(ii) The graded submodule
$S:=\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)s_i=\sum_iU_q^-s_i$ is proper, and the quotient
$\tilde L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/S$ is nonzero, has finite-dimensional
label-weight spaces, and is integrable ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]).

(iii) Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of highest weight
$\lambda$ is a quotient of $\tilde L(\lambda)$.

No commutation between divided powers $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$ of distinct indices
with $a_{ij}\ne0$ is assumed anywhere.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

Let $R=\mathbb C\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$, $K=\mathbb C((\hbar))$, $q=e^\hbar$, and $q_i=e^{d_i\hbar}$ for a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum. Let $H^+=U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+$, $\langle V\rangle$ and the shuffle product be as in [[def-formal-quantum-shuffle-borel-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], and put $H^-=T(V^*)/J_-$ using [[lem-quantum-serre-sums-vanish-in-the-formal-quantum-shuffle-algebra]]. Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), used only through the formal embedding theorem. For an indeterminate $z$, let $H_z^\pm$ be the algebras over $\mathbb C(z)$ presented by the separate symmetric quantum Serre relations, with parameters $z_i=z^{d_i}$.

(i) Each $H^\pm[\pm\alpha]$ is finite free over $R$, and
$$\operatorname{rank}_R H^\pm[\pm\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C}U(\mathfrak n^\pm)[\pm\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C(z)}H_z^\pm[\pm\alpha].$$
Every family of homogeneous lifts of a basis of the classical component is an $R$-basis. Likewise, homogeneous word expressions with coefficients rational in $z$, regular at $z=1$, which reduce to a classical component basis form a basis of the corresponding generic component. In particular, for a supplied ordered homogeneous basis of $\mathfrak n^\pm$, ordered monomials in any such regular lifts form a generic PBW basis.

(ii) Both formal halves are graded braided Hopf algebras. Their generators are primitive, their counits kill positive height, and their tensor squares use
$$ (u\otimes v)(u'\otimes v')=q^{-\langle\deg u',\deg v\rangle}uu'\otimes vv',\qquad \langle\epsilon_i,\epsilon_j\rangle=d_i a_{ij},$$
with negative degrees for $H^-$. The word pairing restricts and descends to a nondegenerate $K$-valued pairing $H^+\times H^-$ with $\langle e_i,f_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}/(\hbar d_i)$ and $\langle1,1\rangle=1$. It is zero on unequal opposite degrees and satisfies the braided Hopf adjunctions
$$\langle x,yy'\rangle=\sum\langle x_{(1)},y\rangle\langle x_{(2)},y'\rangle,\qquad\langle xx',y\rangle=\sum\langle x,y_{(1)}\rangle\langle x',y_{(2)}\rangle.$$
The generic halves have the same braided Hopf structures and a nondegenerate $\mathbb C(z)$-valued pairing normalized by $\langle e_i,f_j\rangle_z=\delta_{ij}/(z_i-z_i^{-1})$. Thus opposite graded components are dual. All generic assertions also hold for the corresponding $\mathbb Q(z)$-presentations and their rational pairing, with the PBW lift clause using bases of the rational classical Serre form.

derivations.claim: **Simultaneous induction and the base layer.** Replace the assertions by the following height-$r$ induction statements: X$(r)$: the triple of $U_A^-$ is integrally balanced in every degree of height $\le r$ with bar-invariant global lifts $G_\infty(b)$ forming an $A$-basis and $\mathbb Z$-intersection $\mathbb Z\mathcal B(\infty)$; Y$(r)$: the same for every $V_A(\lambda)$ with lifts $G_\lambda(b)$ and intersection $\mathbb Z\mathcal B(\lambda)$; Z$(r)$: the negative-half membership $G_\infty(b)\in I_{(i,1)}^A$ whenever $\tilde e_ib\ne0$, for every new degree of height $\le r$; and the derived clause D$(r)$: for the new degrees, the based-quotient compatibility $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=0$ if and only if $\pi_\lambda(b)=0$, and $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=G_\lambda(\pi_\lambda(b))$ otherwise. For $r=0$ the degree component is $A\cdot1$ or $Av_\lambda$, the charts meet in $\mathbb Z\cdot1$ or $\mathbb Z v_\lambda$, and the stated properties hold by inspection. Assume X, Y, Z, D for all heights $<r$ and fix a degree $\alpha$ of height $r\ge1$.

**The string ideals at height $r$ are balanced.** The induction hypotheses are exactly the input of [F1] at height $r$, so for every $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$ the ideals $I_{(i,n)}^A$ and $J_{(i,n)}^A$ are integrally balanced in degree $-\alpha$, respectively $\lambda-\alpha$, with adapted free bases whose balanced $\mathbb Z$-intersections map isomorphically onto $\mathbb Z(\mathcal B(\infty)\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B(\infty))$ and $\mathbb Z(\mathcal B(\lambda)\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B(\lambda))$. In particular, for each $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B(\infty)$ there is an adapted lift $g\in E_{I_{(i,n)}}:=I_{(i,n)}^A\cap\mathcal L(\infty)\cap\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$ whose residue class in $(I_{(i,n)}^A\cap\mathcal L(\infty))/(I_{(i,n)}^A\cap q\mathcal L(\infty))$ is $b$; these are the only lifts used below.

**Every string lift is bar fixed.** Let $g\in E_I:=I_{(i,n)}^A\cap\mathcal L(\infty)\cap\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$ be any adapted lift. By [F3] the ideal $I_{(i,n)}^A$ is generated over $A$ by bar-fixed divided-word vectors, so write $g=\sum_wa_ww$ with $a_w\in A$ and $\psi(w)=w$; then $g-\psi(g)=\sum_w(a_w-\psi(a_w))w$, and each antisymmetric Laurent polynomial $a_w-\psi(a_w)$ is divisible in $A$ by $q-q^{-1}$, so $h:=\bigl(g-\psi(g)\bigr)/(q-q^{-1})\in I_{(i,n)}^A$. Since $g,\psi(g)\in\mathcal L(\infty)\cap\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$ and $(q-q^{-1})^{-1}=-q(1-q^2)^{-1}\in qA_0$, one gets $h\in q\mathcal L(\infty)$; since $(q-q^{-1})^{-1}=q^{-1}(1-q^{-2})^{-1}\in A_\infty$, one gets $h\in\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$. Thus $h\in E_I$ and $h\in q\mathcal L(\infty)$, so its class in $(I_{(i,n)}^A\cap\mathcal L(\infty))/(I_{(i,n)}^A\cap q\mathcal L(\infty))\cong\mathbb Z(\mathcal B(\infty)\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B(\infty))$ is zero; by injectivity of the balanced residue map of [F2](1) applied to $I_{(i,n)}^A$, $h=0$ and $g=\psi(g)$. The same argument applies to the module ideals $J_{(i,n)}^A$.

**Gluing across colors (Kashiwara’s gluing lemma).** Let $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ lie in $\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\infty)\cap\tilde f_j\mathcal B(\infty)$, and let $G_i(b),G_j(b)\in\mathcal L(\infty)\cap\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$ be the corresponding adapted lifts of $I_{(i,1)}^A$ and $I_{(j,1)}^A$ from step 2.1. Write $b$ as a lowering word with rightmost color $k$ and choose, using [F7], a dominant integral auxiliary label $\lambda$ in the regular datum with $\lambda(h_k)=0$ and all other coordinates larger than the degree bounds. By the kernel statement of [F7], $\ker\pi_\lambda$ in degree $\alpha$ equals the image of $U_q^-F_k$, and $\pi_\lambda(b)=0$: modulo $q$, projection commutes with every lowering operator, while the rightmost $\tilde f_k$ kills the highest class because $\lambda(h_k)=0$. For each of the two lifts, $G_i(b)v_\lambda$ lies in $J_{(i,1)}^A$ by [F3], lies in $q\mathcal L(\lambda)$ because its crystal residue $\pi_\lambda(b)=0$, and lies in $\psi(\mathcal L(\lambda))$ by bar invariance; the balancedness of $J_{(i,1)}^A$ from step 2.1 forces $G_i(b)v_\lambda=0$, and likewise $G_j(b)v_\lambda=0$. Hence $Q:=G_i(b)-G_j(b)$ lies in $U_A^-\cap U_q^-F_k$, in $q\mathcal L(\infty)$ (both lifts have residue $b$), and in $\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$. By the reversal [F4], $Q^\star$ lies in $U_A^-\cap F_kU_q^-\cap q\mathcal L(\infty)\cap\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$; by [F3], $U_A^-\cap F_kU_q^-=I_{(k,1)}^A$; and then the balancedness of $I_{(k,1)}^A$ from step 2.1 again forces $Q^\star=0$, hence $Q=0$.

**Global half lifts and spanning.** For $\alpha\ne0$, [F5] supplies for every $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ a color $i$ and a predecessor $b'\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha+\alpha_i}$ with $b=\tilde f_ib'$, so $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)\cap\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\infty)$ and step 2.1 provides an adapted lift in $I_{(i,1)}^A$; define $G_\infty(b)$ to be this element. Step 3.2 shows the definition does not depend on the chosen color, and two lifts for the same color differ by an element of $E_I\cap q\mathcal L(\infty)=0$ by step 3.1, so $G_\infty(b)$ is well defined and bar invariant. By [F3], every nonempty divided-word generator in degree $-\alpha$ begins with a positive divided power $F_i^{(l)}$ and therefore belongs to $I_{(i,1)}^A$, hence $U_A^-=\sum_{i\in I}I_{(i,1)}^A$ in this degree; by step 2.1 and the lower-height part of the induction, each $I_{(i,1)}^A$ has the free $A$-basis $\{G_\infty(b):b\in\mathcal B(\infty)\cap\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\infty)\}$. Therefore $U_A^-$ in degree $-\alpha$ equals $\sum_{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}}AG_\infty(b)$, and X$(<r)$ supplies the lower-height components, so the family $(G_\infty(b))_b$ spans $U_A^-$ over $A$ in every degree of height $\le r$.

**The half triple is integrally balanced (X$(r)$).** Put $F:=\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}}\mathbb ZG_\infty(b)$; it is a finite free $\mathbb Z$-module contained in $U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)\cap\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$ because the lifts are bar invariant and lie in the adapted integers of the string ideals. It generates $U_A^-$ over $A$ by step 4.1. Its image in $\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ is $\bigoplus_b\mathbb Zb$ by [F6], and its image under $\psi$ is another free $\mathbb Z$-span of the same rank inside the infinity residue; the two images are injective. Applying the chart generation criterion [F2](2) to $M=U_A^-$, $L_0=\mathcal L(\infty)$ and $L_\infty=\psi(\mathcal L(\infty))$ gives that the half triple in degree $-\alpha$ is integrally balanced, with $E=F$ and $E\to(U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty))/(U_A^-\cap q\mathcal L(\infty))$ an isomorphism onto $\bigoplus_b\mathbb Zb$; the same holds in every lower degree by X$(<r)$, so X$(r)$ holds.

**Adapted membership and the top-string transition.** An adapted lift of $I_{(i,n)}^A$ and the global lift with the same residue both lie in the now balanced half intersection; its injectivity identifies them. Hence $I_{(i,n)}^A=\bigoplus_{b\in\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B(\infty)}AG_\infty(b)$ and Z$(r)$ holds. For $\tilde e_ib=0$, put $\varphi=F_i^{(n)}G_\infty(b)$. The relative quotient construction of [F1], transported to the half, provides $e\in E_{I_{(i,n)}}$ with $e-\varphi\in I_{(i,n+1)}^A$ and residue $\tilde f_i^nb$ modulo the higher string residues. Expressing $e$ in the adapted balanced basis, its coefficient at that $n$-position is $1$ and all other $n$-position coefficients are $0$; its remaining coefficients multiply higher-position lifts. Thus $\varphi-G_\infty(\tilde f_i^nb)\in I_{(i,n+1)}^A$, proving (v). This is uniqueness in the quotient charts, rather than an assertion that $\varphi$ itself belongs to the balanced intersection.

**Killed module images vanish.** Fix $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ have $\pi_\lambda(b)=0$. By [F5] choose $i$ with $\tilde e_ib\ne0$; then $b\in\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\infty)$, so $G_\infty(b)\in I_{(i,1)}^A$ by Z$(r)$ and $G_\infty(b)v_\lambda\in J_{(i,1)}^A$ by [F3]. Since its residue $\pi_\lambda(b)$ is zero it lies in $q\mathcal L(\lambda)$, and since $G_\infty(b)$ is bar invariant and $\pi_\lambda$ commutes with $\psi$ it lies in $\psi(\mathcal L(\lambda))$. The balancedness of $J_{(i,1)}^A$ from step 2.1 forces the class of $G_\infty(b)v_\lambda$ in its balanced intersection to be zero, so $G_\infty(b)v_\lambda=0$; this is the local form of Kashiwara’s killed-image lemma.

**The surviving module images.** For $\pi_\lambda(b)\ne0$, the element $G_\infty(b)v_\lambda$ is bar invariant, lies in $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ by the lattice projection of [F5], and its residue in $\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda)$ is $\pi_\lambda(b)$ by the derived clause D$(<r)$ and the operator compatibility of [F5]; the residues $\pi_\lambda(b)$ over the surviving $b$ biject onto $\mathcal B(\lambda)$ by [F5]. These images span $V_A(\lambda)$ over $A$ because $U_A^-$ is spanned by the $G_\infty(b)$ and, by [F3] and step 7.1, $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective with the killed generators contributing zero.

**The module triple is integrally balanced (Y$(r)$).** Let $F_\lambda:=\bigoplus_{b:\pi_\lambda(b)\ne0}\mathbb ZG_\infty(b)v_\lambda$ inside $V_A(\lambda)\cap\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap\psi(\mathcal L(\lambda))$. It generates $V_A(\lambda)$ over $A$ by step 8.1 and its image in $\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda)$ is $\bigoplus_{\beta\in\mathcal B(\lambda)}\mathbb Z\beta$ by the bijection of residues, hence is a free generator group; the bar image is the corresponding free span in $\psi(\mathcal L(\lambda))/q^{-1}\psi(\mathcal L(\lambda))$, injective of the same rank. The chart generation criterion [F2](2), applied to $M=V_A(\lambda)$, $L_0=\mathcal L(\lambda)$, $L_\infty=\psi(\mathcal L(\lambda))$, gives integral balancedness in degree $\lambda-\alpha$ with $E_{\mathbb Z}=\bigoplus_{\pi_\lambda(b)\ne0}\mathbb ZG_\infty(b)v_\lambda$ and residue group $\mathbb Z\mathcal B(\lambda)$; with the induction hypothesis in lower degrees this is Y$(r)$. Uniqueness of the balanced lift identifies each $G_\infty(b)v_\lambda$ with the adapted module lift $G_\lambda(\pi_\lambda(b))$, which also proves (iv) in degree $\alpha$.

**Saturation and the adapted string bases.** The lifts $G_\lambda(\beta)$ for $\beta\in\mathcal B(\lambda)$ now form an $A$-basis of $V_A(\lambda)$ in every degree of height $\le r$, and by [F3] the ideals $J_{(i,n)}^A$ are generated by the images of the corresponding string ideal generators. By the rational string decomposition and crystal partial inverses, the dimension of $F_i^nV(\lambda)$ is the number of surviving positions at least $n$. The adapted basis of $J_{(i,n)}^A$ lies in that field space and has exactly this many independent lifts, so it spans the field space. Its intersection with the full global $A$-lattice therefore equals the $A$-span of the adapted lifts $\{G_\lambda(\beta):\beta\in\mathcal B(\lambda)\cap\tilde f_i^n\mathcal B(\lambda)\}$, which is exactly $J_{(i,n)}^A$; this proves the saturation identity and the displayed free decompositions of (iii) for the module, and the half decompositions were proved in step 6.1.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1 and 2.1 set up the induction and produce the balanced string ideals; steps 3.1 and 3.2 prove bar invariance and the gluing of string lifts; steps 4.1 and 5.1 construct the global half basis, its chart injections and X$(r)$; step 6.1 proves Z$(r)$ and the exact top-string transition (v); steps 7.1, 8.1, 9.1 and 10.1 prove Y$(r)$, the projection rule (iv), the module saturation and the adapted decompositions (iii) for both halves. The ranks in (ii) are the field dimensions computed by [F5] rank by rank, with the classical PBW identification supplied by [F8] and its stated Choice hypothesis; the dimension count is finite in each root degree because only finitely many compositions occur. This closes the induction in every degree and proves (i)-(v); the Choice use is confined to [C1].

risk_review.notes: Checked all twelve steps and every cited current supplier. The height-zero unit/top triples are balanced over Z, and lower-height X/Y/Z plus quotient compatibility are exactly the string-ideal induction inputs. For a string lift, (g-bar g)/(q-q^-1) lies in the integral ideal, in qL0 and in the infinity chart; balanced injectivity forces bar invariance. The gluing proof chooses an explicit auxiliary lambda with one zero coroot coordinate and all others above the degree bound; crystal projection kills the corresponding lowering word, so both ideal lifts lie in the right kernel U^-F_k. Reversal sends it to the balanced left ideal F_kU^-, forcing equality. The first divided block in every nonempty divided word gives integral spanning; both residue injections give the global half triple, and quotient-chart uniqueness gives the exact top-string transition modulo the next ideal. Killed images vanish in balanced module ideals; surviving images give a basis by crystal projection. The adapted field span and the full global A-basis establish saturation. I corrected F4 to show the actual right-ideal reversal target U_A^- intersect U_q^-F_k^n, replaced undefined tilde-e-prime by e-prime, and stated the gluing zero image in the residue rather than acting on a residue class as a field vector. Statement and all consumer conclusions remain intact. Independently read the full Kashiwara induction/gluing/killed-image proof on printed pp.512-516 (PDF48-52). (vi) **Quasi-R normalization.** In each degree $\nu$ let $(x_a),(y_b)$ be bases of $U_q^+[\nu]$ and $U_q^-[-\nu]$ and let $\Theta_\nu=\sum_a x_a\otimes y^a$ be the $D$-coevaluation, $y^a$ the $D$-dual basis. In particular, writing $[n]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{r=1}^n(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(r-1)})$ (the geometric-sum factorial of the receiving page),
$$\Theta_{n\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n[n]_{q_i^2}!\,E_i^{(n)}\otimes F_i^{(n)},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \Theta_{\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})\,E_i\otimes F_i.$$

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with its generated
subalgebras $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ and root gradings
$U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ of
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]
($Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$, height $\operatorname{ht}$ of
[[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]). Fix $i\in I$ and
write $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, so that $K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j$ and
$q_i-q_i^{-1}\ne0$.

For every $P\in U_q^-$ there exist unique elements $Q,R\in U_q^-$ with

$$E_iP-PE_i=\frac{K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}.$$

Define the **Kashiwara skew derivations** $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ by

$$e_i'(P):=R\qquad\text{and}\qquad e_i''(P):=Q .$$

Thus $e_i'$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i^{-1}$ and
$e_i''$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i$ in the
commutator with $E_i$. The maps have the following properties, all proved in
the Verification below.

(a) $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, vanish on $1$, and
$e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$ for all $j\in I$.

(b) (Twisted Leibniz rules) For homogeneous $x,y\in U_q^-$, with the actual
weight $\operatorname{wt}(x)\in Q$ of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]],
$$e_i'(xy)=e_i'(x)y+q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i'(y),\qquad e_i''(xy)=e_i''(x)y+q_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i''(y).$$

(c) (Commutation with the generators) For all $j\in I$ and all $y\in U_q^-$,
$$e_i'(F_jy)=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i'(y)+\delta_{ij}y,\qquad e_i''(F_jy)=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i''(y)+\delta_{ij}y,$$

equivalently $e_i'F_j=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'+\delta_{ij}$ and
$e_i''F_j=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_je_i''+\delta_{ij}$ as operators on $U_q^-$.

(d) (Grading, height and nilpotence) For every $\nu\in Q_+$,

$$e_i'\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr),\ e_i''\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr)\ \subseteq\ U_q^-[ -(\nu-\alpha_i)],$$

the right-hand side being $0$ when $\nu-\alpha_i\notin Q_+$. In particular both
maps raise the actual weight by $\alpha_i$, lower the positive height by one,
and are locally nilpotent: $(e_i')^{k}(P)=(e_i'')^{k}(P)=0$ for $k$ larger than
the height of the degree of a homogeneous $P$.

(e) (Bar compatibility) Let $\psi$ be the semilinear algebra involution
$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, $E_i\mapsto E_i$, $F_i\mapsto F_i$, $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].
Then $e_i''=\psi\,e_i'\,\psi$ on $U_q^-$.

The commutator construction also fixes the orientation: the
$K_i^{-1}$-coefficient is $e_i'$ and the $K_i$-coefficient is $e_i''$. The
twists $q_i^{\pm\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}$ in (b) are the twists
of the corresponding coefficient maps of the negative-half coproduct in the
source's dictionary; the explicit commutator computation used here is the
definition of record, and no imaginary-simple-root convention is needed, since
every Cartan datum of this library has $a_{ii}=2$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum with
$a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]),
let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), and let
$e_i',e_i''$ be the skew derivations of
[[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]].

(i) **One step.** If $x\in U_q^-[-\nu]$ with $\nu\ne0$ satisfies
$e_i'(x)=0$ for all $i\in I$, then $x=0$.

(ii) **Iterated separation.** For every $0\ne x\in U_q^-[-\nu]$ there is a
sequence $i_1,\dots,i_k\in I$ with $\nu=\alpha_{i_1}+\cdots+\alpha_{i_k}$ (the
multiset is uniquely determined by $\nu$, because the simple roots freely
generate $Q$, and $k=\operatorname{ht}(\nu)$) such that
$e_{i_k}'\cdots e_{i_2}'e_{i_1}'(x)\ne0$. Here the composite is read with the
rightmost factor applied first, so the first chosen derivation $e_{i_1}'$ acts
first; equivalently, the common kernel, on $U_q^-[-\nu]$, of all composites
$e_{i_1}'\cdots e_{i_k}'$ over all such sequences is zero.

The same statements hold with $e_i''$ in place of $e_i'$. This separation property is used by the crystal development and the categorification pairing.

Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and defining ideal of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and write $K_i=K_{d_i h_i}$. Let $\Delta:T\to T\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}T$ and $\varepsilon:T\to\mathbb Q(q)$ be the algebra homomorphisms determined by

$$\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h,\quad \Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i,\quad \Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i,\quad \varepsilon(K_h)=1,\quad\varepsilon(E_i)=\varepsilon(F_i)=0.$$

Let $S:T\to T$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear algebra anti-homomorphism determined by

$$S(K_h)=K_{-h},\qquad S(E_i)=-E_iK_i,\qquad S(F_i)=-K_i^{-1}F_i.$$

Then

$$\Delta(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}\otimes T+T\otimes I_{\mathrm{DJ}},\qquad \varepsilon(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})=0,\qquad S(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}.$$

Hence these maps descend to $U_q(\mathfrak g)=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and make it a Hopf algebra over $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[def-bialgebra-counit-and-antipode]]): $\Delta$ is coassociative, $\varepsilon$ is a counit, and

$$m(S\otimes\operatorname{id})\Delta=\eta\circ\varepsilon=m(\operatorname{id}\otimes S)\Delta.$$

The antipode $S$ is unique for this multiplication, unit, coproduct and counit ([[lem-an-antipode-is-unique]]), and its square satisfies

$$S^2(E_i)=q_i^{-2}E_i,\qquad S^2(F_i)=q_i^{2}F_i,\qquad S^2(K_h)=K_h.$$

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum and let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with $q_i=q^{d_i}$, $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, coproduct $\Delta$, counit $\varepsilon$ and antipode $S$ as in [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]. Write $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A$, with generators $E_i^{(r)},F_i^{(r)},K_h^{\pm1},T_{i,c,t}$, be the Lusztig divided-power form of the receiving page. $$K_h^{L}E_i^{L}=v^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_i^{L}K_h^{L},\qquad K_h^{L}F_i^{L}=v^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_i^{L}K_h^{L},$$

$$\Delta_L E_i^{L}=E_i^{L}\otimes1+K_i^{L}\otimes E_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L F_i^{L}=F_i^{L}\otimes(K_i^{L})^{-1}+1\otimes F_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L K_h^{L}=K_h^{L}\otimes K_h^{L}.$$

After the separate coefficient-renaming isomorphism $\rho:v\mapsto q$, $K_h^L\mapsto K_h$, this transport is $\varphi=\psi\rho$, with $\psi$ the library bar involution. It carries the source integral form onto $U_A$, fixes divided powers, inverts toral generators and fixes $T_{i,c,t}$. One must not apply the library bar a second time to the already transported parameter $v=q^{-1}$.

Equivalently the source coproduct is the opposite of the fixed library coproduct after parameter transport: the flip of the transported source coproduct is $\Delta$. $$(x_1\otimes x_2)(y_1\otimes y_2)=q^{-\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}x_1y_1\otimes x_2y_2$$

$$S(K_h)=K_{-h},\qquad S(E_i)=-E_iK_i,\qquad S(F_i)=-K_i^{-1}F_i.$$

$$\Delta(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}\otimes T+T\otimes I_{\mathrm{DJ}},\qquad \varepsilon(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})=0,\qquad S(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}.$$

Hence these maps descend to $U_q(\mathfrak g)=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and make it a Hopf algebra over $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[def-bialgebra-counit-and-antipode]]): $\Delta$ is coassociative, $\varepsilon$ is a counit, and

$$m(S\otimes\operatorname{id})\Delta=\eta\circ\varepsilon=m(\operatorname{id}\otimes S)\Delta.$$

The antipode $S$ is unique for this multiplication, unit, coproduct and counit ([[lem-an-antipode-is-unique]]), and its square satisfies

$$S^2(E_i)=q_i^{-2}E_i,\qquad S^2(F_i)=q_i^{2}F_i,\qquad S^2(K_h)=K_h.$$

For the fixed library coproduct use the **diagonal root-height completion**
$$\widehat C=\prod_{
u\in Q_+}U^+[
u]\otimes U^-[-
u],$$
with multiplication $(AB)_
u=\sum_{ eta+\gamma=
u}A_ eta B_\gamma$; each component sum is finite because $I$ is finite and the root coefficients of $ eta,\gamma\in Q_+$ are nonnegative integers. For intertwining with $\Delta$, use the ambient completed tensor square obtained from the source completion by the exact presentation map of [[lem-lusztig-and-kashiwara-normalizations-match-by-root-color]] ( $v=q^{-1}$, $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}$ ) followed by the tensor flip; equivalently, every generator identity is read coefficientwise in the root grading. The tensor orientation is **positive first, negative second** ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]).

A family $A\in\widehat C$ **acts** on $m_\mu\otimes n_\eta$ by its finite sum whenever $U^+[
u]m_\mu\otimes U^-[-
u]n_\eta$ vanishes for all sufficiently high $
u$. This holds if the first factor has finite-union bounded-above support, or if the second factor is a lowest module with bounded-below support. For both factors in the finite-weight-space category $\mathcal O_{\mathrm{int}}$ the relevant fixed total-weight subspace is finite dimensional, and every tail beyond a finite degree acts as $0$ there. An infinite series is not evaluated on a two-sided-unbounded pair without this explicit finiteness condition.

This completion and the normalization $\Theta_0=1$ are field-level data of the based-module theory of [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]]; no universal $R$-matrix, no braiding and no integral coefficient property is asserted here.

Let $
u\in Q_+$, let $(u_a)$ be a field basis of $U_q^+[
u]$ and $(v^a)$ its $D$-dual basis in $U_q^-[-
u]$ with respect to the normalized Drinfeld pairing of [[lem-the-drinfeld-hopf-pairing-is-nondegenerate-in-each-root-degree]] (so $D(u_a,v^b)=\delta_a^b$), and set
$$\Theta_
u:=\sum_au_a\otimes v^a\in U_q^+[
u]\otimes U_q^-[-
u]\subseteq\widehat C,$$
the ambient root-height completion of [[def-root-height-completion-for-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiners]]. Then $\Theta_
u$ is independent of the chosen basis of $U_q^+[
u]$, and $\Theta_0=1\otimes1$. The family $(\Theta_
u)_
u$ has finite-dimensional homogeneous components and defines a vectorwise finite action under the exact finiteness hypotheses of the completion definition. Its degree-$
u$ action shifts a label pair $(\mu,\eta)$ to $(\mu+
u,\eta-
u)$, preserving the total weight, and on finite-weight-space $O_{\mathrm{int}}$ pairs every fixed total-weight space has a uniform finite tail bound beyond which all components act as $0$. No integral algebra coefficients are asserted, and the positive-height components have no same-weight-pair diagonal term.

Let $D$ be the normalized Drinfeld pairing of [[def-drinfeld-hopf-pairing-between-positive-and-negative-quantum-halves]], $D(x,y)=d_\nu^{-1}B_K(\iota x,y)$ on $U_q^+[\nu]\times U_q^-[-\nu]$, where $B_K$ is the normalized Kashiwara half form of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]]. Then:

(i) $D$ is homogeneous, descends to the actual Serre quotients $U_q^\pm$, and is nondegenerate (equivalently perfect) over $\mathbb Q(q)$ in every finite root degree; its rank-one values are $D(E_i,F_j)=\delta_{ij}(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{-1}$ and $D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}/([n]_i!(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n)$.

(ii) $D$ equals the formal generic Hopf pairing on the simple-root Borel extensions with the exact generator and toral normalization, so that
$$D(xx',y)=\sum D(x,y_{(1)})D(x',y_{(2)}),\qquad D(x,yy')=\sum D(x_{(1)},y)D(x_{(2)},y'),$$
with $\Delta y$ on the negative Borel and $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}x$ on the positive Borel, including their toral factors.

These are field identities; no divided-power integral perfectness and no $A$-valuedness of $D$ is asserted.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum and let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with $q_i=q^{d_i}$, $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, coproduct $\Delta$, counit $\varepsilon$ and antipode $S$ as in [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]. Write $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A$, with generators $E_i^{(r)},F_i^{(r)},K_h^{\pm1},T_{i,c,t}$, be the Lusztig divided-power form of the receiving page. On the source side take Lusztig's presentation over $\mathbb Q(v)$, where $v$ is an indeterminate and $v_i=v^{d_i}$; the transport below sends $v_i$ to $q_i^{-1}$: generators $E_i^{L},F_i^{L},K_h^{L}$, the toral relations $K_h^{L}K_{h'}^{L}=K_{h+h'}^{L}$, $K_0^{L}=1$, the toral-action relations
$$K_h^{L}E_i^{L}=v^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_i^{L}K_h^{L},\qquad K_h^{L}F_i^{L}=v^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_i^{L}K_h^{L},$$
the mixed relations $E_i^{L}F_j^{L}-F_j^{L}E_i^{L}=\delta_{ij}(K_i^{L}-(K_i^{L})^{-1})/(v_i-v_i^{-1})$, and the Serre relations with $v_i$-Gaussian binomial coefficients; let $\Delta_L$ be the source coproduct on generators
$$\Delta_L E_i^{L}=E_i^{L}\otimes1+K_i^{L}\otimes E_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L F_i^{L}=F_i^{L}\otimes(K_i^{L})^{-1}+1\otimes F_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L K_h^{L}=K_h^{L}\otimes K_h^{L}.$$
Let $B_K$ be the normalized Kashiwara half form on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]], with skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$ of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], and let $\psi$ be the bar involution of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]. Then:

(i) **Parameter transport.** The assignment $\varphi(v)=q^{-1}$, $\varphi(E_i^L)=E_i$, $\varphi(F_i^L)=F_i$, $\varphi(K_h^L)=K_{-h}$ defines an algebra isomorphism semilinear for the field isomorphism $\mathbb Q(v)\to\mathbb Q(q)$, $v\mapsto q^{-1}$. Its inverse sends $q\mapsto v^{-1}$ and $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}^L$, fixing the root generators. After the separate coefficient-renaming isomorphism $\rho:v\mapsto q$, $K_h^L\mapsto K_h$, this transport is $\varphi=\psi\rho$, with $\psi$ the library bar involution. It carries the source integral form onto $U_A$, fixes divided powers, inverts toral generators and fixes $T_{i,c,t}$. One must not apply the library bar a second time to the already transported parameter $v=q^{-1}$.

(ii) **Coproduct transport.** On all of the source algebra, $(\varphi\otimes\varphi)\circ\Delta_L=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\circ\varphi$, where $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}=\mathrm{flip}\circ\Delta$. Equivalently the source coproduct is the opposite of the fixed library coproduct after parameter transport: the flip of the transported source coproduct is $\Delta$. In particular, with the barred coproduct $\bar\Delta(u):=(\psi\otimes\psi)\Delta(\psi(u))$, an element of the completed tensor square satisfying the source intertwining convention for $\Delta_L$ has a transport-flip that satisfies the library convention $\Delta(u)\Theta=\Theta\bar\Delta(u)$; this is the convention under which the normalized family of (vi) is read.

(iii) **The abstract half and its twisted product.** Transporting $\theta_i\mapsto F_i$ sends the source half $\mathbf f$ to $U_q^-$, the divided powers $\theta_i^{(n)}$ to $F_i^{(n)}$, and the source twisted coproduct multiplication $(x_1\otimes x_2)(y_1\otimes y_2)=v^{\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}x_1y_1\otimes x_2y_2$ to
$$(x_1\otimes x_2)(y_1\otimes y_2)=q^{-\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}x_1y_1\otimes x_2y_2$$
on $U_q^-\otimes U_q^-$; the coefficient extraction $e_i'(F_jQ)=\delta_{ij}Q+q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'(Q)$ of the transported twisted coproduct agrees with the library skew derivation $e_i'$.

(iv) **The half form up to the root-color factor.** On the homogeneous degree $\nu=\sum_i\nu_i\alpha_i$ the source form and the normalized Kashiwara form are related by
$$B_L=C_\nu\,B_K,\qquad C_\nu=\prod_i(1-q_i^2)^{-\nu_i},$$
a color-degree scaling which is a unit congruent to $1$ modulo $q$ and is not a single scalar on the whole half; for $P,Q$ of different degrees both sides vanish. In the rank-one subalgebra $B_L(F_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=\prod_{r=1}^n(1-q_i^{2r})^{-1}$.

(v) **The normalized Drinfeld pairing.** Let $\iota:U_q^+\to U_q^-$ be the algebra isomorphism $E_i\mapsto F_i$. On homogeneous elements of opposite degrees set
$$D(x,y)=d_\nu^{-1}B_K(\iota x,y),\qquad d_\nu=\prod_i(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{\nu_i}\ \ (\deg x=\nu,\ \deg y=-\nu),$$
and set $D(x,y)=0$ for degrees not opposite. Then $D$ is a well-defined homogeneous pairing, perfect on every finite graded piece, and $D(E_i,F_j)=\delta_{ij}/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$; the pairing with generator value $1$ is the $B_K$-transport $B_K(\iota x,y)$. Its divided-power values are
$$D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=\frac{q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}}{[n]_i!\,(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n}.$$

(vi) **Quasi-R normalization.** In each degree $\nu$ let $(x_a),(y_b)$ be bases of $U_q^+[\nu]$ and $U_q^-[-\nu]$ and let $\Theta_\nu=\sum_a x_a\otimes y^a$ be the $D$-coevaluation, $y^a$ the $D$-dual basis. Then $\Theta_\nu$ is the transported, tensor-flipped source quasi-R component: the source coefficient of Lusztig's printed $\Theta$ is $(-1)^{\mathrm{ht}\,\nu}\prod_iv_i^{\nu_i}$ times the $B_L$-coevaluation, and after parameter transport and flip this scalar equals $d_\nu$, the scalar by which the $D$-coevaluation differs from the $B_K$-coevaluation. In particular, writing $[n]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{r=1}^n(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(r-1)})$ (the geometric-sum factorial of the receiving page),
$$\Theta_{n\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n[n]_{q_i^2}!\,E_i^{(n)}\otimes F_i^{(n)},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \Theta_{\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})\,E_i\otimes F_i.$$

derivations.claim: **The barred equation.** Bar the intertwining equation with $B=\psi\otimes\psi$: from $\Delta(u)\Theta=\Theta\overline\Delta(u)$ and [F2] one gets $\overline\Delta(\psi(u))\,\overline\Theta=\overline\Theta\,\Delta(\psi(u))$ for every $u$, i.e. after replacing $u$ by $\psi(u)$, $\overline\Delta(u)\overline\Theta=\overline\Theta\Delta(u)$. Inverting the original equation in the convolution algebra [F3] gives $\Theta^{-1}\Delta(u)=\overline\Delta(u)\Theta^{-1}$; applying the algebra automorphism $B$ and using [F2] turns this into $\Delta(\psi(u))B(\Theta^{-1})=B(\Theta^{-1})\overline\Delta(\psi(u))$.

**The coproduct factorizations by duality.** Fix degrees $\gamma,\eta$. In the corresponding component of $\Delta x$, $x\in U^+[\gamma+\eta]$, remove the middle torus to write the coefficient tensor as $x_1\otimes K_{-\eta}x_2$, with $|x_1|=\eta$, $|x_2|=\gamma$. The Hopf adjunction for $D$ gives $\sum D(x_1,z)D(x_2,y)=q^{(\eta,\gamma)}D(x,yz)$ for $y\in U^-[-\gamma]$, $z\in U^-[-\eta]$: in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}x$ the toral pairing is $D(K_{-\eta},K_\gamma)=q^{-(\eta,\gamma)}$. Contract the first two root slots of $(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta$ with these two functionals; the result is $q^{(\eta,\gamma)}yz$. The proposed right side has the same contraction, since $x_2K_{-\eta}=q^{(\eta,\gamma)}K_{-\eta}x_2$ and the two coevaluations contract to $y,z$. This proves the first identity by perfectness. For the second, the degree component of $\Delta u$ for $u\in U^-[-\gamma-\eta]$ is $u_1K_\eta\otimes u_2$. The other Hopf adjunction gives $\sum D(a,u_1)D(b,u_2)=D(ab,u)$ for $a\in U^+[\gamma]$, $b\in U^+[\eta]$; the first pairing with $u_1K_\eta$ has no additional scalar, by the counit term of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}a$. Contracting the last two root slots on each proposed side therefore gives $ab$. This proves the second identity. All tests are in finite homogeneous components; the toral directions are retained, not discarded.

**Identification of the inverse.** Put $Y:=B(\Theta^{-1})=\overline{\Theta^{-1}}$. Step 1.1 shows $\Delta(v)Y=Y\overline\Delta(v)$ for every $v$, and $Y_0=B(\Theta_0)=1$; by the uniqueness clause of [F1], $Y=\Theta$, hence $\Theta^{-1}=B(\Theta)=\overline\Theta$. The inverse is taken in the same positive-first/negative-second completion, because the convolution algebra of [F3] is closed under inversion and $B$ is an automorphism of it; no opposite tensor completion is used.

**Rank-one check in every degree.** Put $t_n=[n]_{q_i^2}!=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}[n]_i!$. The Gaussian coproduct expansions are $\Delta(E_i^{(n)})=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=n}q_i^{\gamma\eta}E_i^{(\eta)}\otimes K_i^{-\eta}E_i^{(\gamma)}$ and $\Delta(F_i^{(n)})=\sum_{\gamma+\eta=n}q_i^{-\gamma\eta}F_i^{(\gamma)}K_i^\eta\otimes F_i^{(\eta)}$. Also $\binom n\gamma_i t_\gamma t_\eta=q_i^{-\gamma\eta}t_n$. In (ii)'s first right side, toral crossing $E_i^{(\gamma)}K_i^{-\eta}=q_i^{2\gamma\eta}K_i^{-\eta}E_i^{(\gamma)}$ and divided-power multiplication produce the coefficient $(q_i-q_i^{-1})^nt_nq_i^{\gamma\eta}$. In the second right side, no toral crossing is needed and the coefficient is $(q_i-q_i^{-1})^nt_nq_i^{-\gamma\eta}$. These are precisely the two left-side coproduct coefficients.

**The barred coproduct identity.** Let $r(u)$ be the negative-half twisted coproduct obtained from $\Delta u$ by removing $K$-factors, with tensor multiplication twisted by $q^{-(\beta,\gamma)}$. Its bar counterpart satisfies $\bar r(u)_{\eta,\gamma}=q^{(\eta,\gamma)}\operatorname{flip}(r(u)_{\gamma,\eta})$: both sides send $F_i$ to $F_i\otimes1+1\otimes F_i$, and the scalar twist verifies multiplicativity on homogeneous products. In $\overline\Delta u$, moving the torus to the left contributes $q^{-(\eta,\gamma)}$ and cancels this factor. Thus, after removing the middle torus $K_{-\gamma}$, the $(\eta,\gamma)$ coefficient of $\overline\Delta u$ is the flip of $r(u)_{\gamma,\eta}$. The Hopf multiplication adjunction used in step 1.2 now shows that contraction of the last two root slots of $(\mathrm{id}\otimes\overline\Delta)\Theta$ gives $ab$, with $a$ testing degree $\gamma$ and $b$ degree $\eta$. The same contraction of $(\Theta_\gamma)_{13}K_{-\gamma}^{(2)}(\Theta_\eta)_{12}$ gives $ab$. Perfectness proves (iv).

**The cocycle identity.** Summing (ii)'s first identity, and noting that the middle torus commutes with every outer $(\Theta_\eta)_{13}$, gives $((\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id})\Theta)\Theta_{12}=\Theta_{23}(\sum_\eta(\Theta_\eta)_{13}K_{-\eta}^{(2)})\Theta_{12}$. By (iv) the last two factors are $(\mathrm{id}\otimes\overline\Delta)\Theta$. Applying $\Delta(y)\Theta=\Theta\overline\Delta(y)$ in the last two positions to each second-factor coefficient $y$ of $\Theta$ gives $\Theta_{23}(\mathrm{id}\otimes\overline\Delta)\Theta=((\mathrm{id}\otimes\Delta)\Theta)\Theta_{23}$. This proves (iii). All operations are coefficientwise in the threefold completion, or finite on the stated admissible vectors. No middle torus is commuted through a $(\Theta_\gamma)_{23}$ term.

**Conclusion and normalization.** Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (i); step 1.2 proves (ii) with the degree-$\alpha_i$ instances and step 2.2 verifies it independently in rank one to all degrees; step 2.3 proves (iv); step 3.1 proves the cocycle identity (iii). The equation $\Delta(u)X=X\overline\Delta(u)$ is homogeneous and linear in $X$, so every nonzero scalar multiple of $\Theta$ satisfies it with $\Theta_0$ scaled equally, and only the normalization $\Theta_0=1$ selects $\Theta$; all computations are at the field level and involve no integrality, while the finite-support hypotheses of [F3] are checked before any completed series is evaluated.

citations.quote:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb Q(q)$, let $M\subseteq V$ be an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-submodule spanning $V$, and let $L_0,L_\infty$ be free full rational chart lattices over $A_0,A_\infty$ (as for a based module in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]]). Put
$$L_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0,\qquad L_{\mathbb Z}^-:=M\cap L_\infty,\qquad E_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty.$$
The **integral triple** $(M,L_0,L_\infty)$ is **balanced** if the canonical $\mathbb Z$-linear map
$$E_{\mathbb Z}\longrightarrow L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}=(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$$
is an isomorphism. Its inverse is the **integral globalization map** on the integral residue subgroup. **Rational balancedness** is the corresponding isomorphism $\mathbb Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}\to L_0/qL_0$, after extending the integral subgroup by $\mathbb Q$. In the applications of this page the integral subgroup is $\mathbb Z B$ for the lower global family $B$, and its globalization gives the lower lifts $G(b)$.

The two-chart lemma of this page proves $M\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$, $L_{\mathbb Z}\cong\mathbb Z[q]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$ and $L_{\mathbb Z}^-\cong\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$. If $E_{\mathbb Z}$ has a finite $\mathbb Z$-basis $B_E$ whose rational residue classes are a basis of $L_0/qL_0$, these lifts give bases of $M,L_0,L_\infty$ over $A,A_0,A_\infty$ respectively. Thus $A$-freeness of $M$ is a conclusion from integral balancedness together with a proved free integral residue basis; it is not automatic for an arbitrary not-finitely-generated $\mathbb Z$-submodule. All definitions apply componentwise to the finite root or label spaces.

Let $\psi$ (the bar involution) and $\tau$ (the contravariant anti-involution) be
the semilinear maps of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]], so
that $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$
and $\tau(q)=q^{-1}$, $\tau(E_i)=F_i$, $\tau(F_i)=E_i$, $\tau(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$,
with $\tau$ anti-multiplicative. Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A$ be
the Lusztig divided-power integral form with its generators $E_i^{(r)}$,
$F_i^{(r)}$, $K_h^{\pm1}$ and toral binomials $T_{i,c,t}$
([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]). Then $\psi(U_A)=U_A$ and
$\tau(U_A)=U_A$. Explicitly, on the generators,

$$\psi(E_i^{(r)})=E_i^{(r)},\quad \psi(F_i^{(r)})=F_i^{(r)},\quad \psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1},\quad \psi(T_{i,c,t})=T_{i,c,t},$$

$$\tau(E_i^{(r)})=F_i^{(r)},\quad \tau(F_i^{(r)})=E_i^{(r)},\quad \tau(K_h)=K_h^{-1},\quad \tau(T_{i,c,t})=T_{i,c,t}.$$

In particular both maps restrict to bijections of $U_A$: $\psi$ to a semilinear
algebra involution of $U_A$ and $\tau$ to a semilinear anti-involution of
$U_A$, while $q^{\pm1}\in A$ keeps all coefficients in $A$. These are the two
involutions under which the bar lattice and the contravariant duality of the
later constructions are taken; neither formula is the Chevalley involution
$\omega$, which changes signs, exchanges the two halves and is treated in
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].
No choice is used.

Fix $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ and the crystal limiting ring $A_0\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ of [[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]], and put $A_\infty:=\psi(A_0)$, the image of $A_0$ under the semilinear involution $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, i.e. the ring of rational functions regular at $q=\infty$; $A_0$ and $A_\infty$ are the rational local rings at $0$ and at infinity, and the integral affine chart coordinate rings are $\mathbb Z[q]$ and $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$.

Let $M$ be one of $U_q^-$ or $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ for $\lambda\in P^+$. Equip $M$ with the bar involution $\psi$ of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]: on $U_q^-$ the semilinear algebra involution with $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$; on $V(\lambda)$ the induced semilinear involution determined by $Pv_\lambda\mapsto\psi(P)v_\lambda$, well defined by the highest-module presentation: its negative-half kernel is $\sum_iU_q^-F_i^{\lambda(h_i)+1}$, preserved by $\psi$ because every $F_i$ is fixed ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]). Equivalently the full highest-vector relations are bar stable: $E_i$ is fixed, the singular divided powers are fixed, and $\psi(K_h-q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle})=-q^{-\langle\lambda,h\rangle}K_{-h}(K_h-q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle})$. Hence the quotient involution is compatible with the algebra action and fixes $v_\lambda$. Let $M_A\subseteq M$ be the divided-power integral form: $M_A=U_A^-$ for $M=U_q^-$, and $M_A=V_A(\lambda):=U_A^-v_\lambda$ for $M=V(\lambda)$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]); both are $\psi$-stable. Let $L$ be the Kashiwara crystal lattice of $M$ over $A_0$: $L=\mathcal L(\infty)$ for $U_q^-$ and $L=\mathcal L(\lambda)$ for $V(\lambda)$ ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]]).

Define the **bar lattice** $L^-:=\psi(L)$, an $A_\infty$-submodule of $M$, and the **balanced part** $E:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$.

The definition keeps three structures on the same $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space strictly separate: the $A$-module $M_A$, which is not assumed free and not claimed to be contained in $L$; the free $A_0$-module $L$; and the free $A_\infty$-module $L^-$. No equality $L^-=L$, no inclusion $M_A\subseteq L$, no freeness of $M_A$ and no identification $E=M_A$ are asserted; freeness is a conclusion of the balanced-triple construction on this page, whereas $E$ is a $\mathbb Z$-module of global lifts and is not equal to the Laurent lattice $M_A$. The bar lattice is not the form-dual (upper) lattice, which is defined later on this page. The intersections $M_A\cap L$ and $M_A\cap L^-$ are respectively $\mathbb Z[q]$- and $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$-modules, generally not $A$-modules. The balanced part $E$ is a $\mathbb Z$-module; its Laurent extension $A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E$ is the full integral module once globalization is proved.

More generally a **based integrable module** $(M,B)$ here means exactly: $B$ is a homogeneous field basis; $M_A=\bigoplus_bAb$ is $U_A$-stable; the semilinear involution fixing $B$ is compatible with the algebra action; and $L_0=\bigoplus_bA_0b$ with residue $B$ is a crystal local basis at $0$. These are the four conditions of Lusztig 27.1.2(a)–(d) after the transport $v=q^{-1}$, together with the integrable extension used by Bao–Wang. Such data do not automatically imply an integral $\Theta$-action on an arbitrary based pair. A **based subobject** is a $U$-submodule spanned by a subset of $B$; a **based quotient** is its quotient with the complementary basis images. Based morphisms send $B$ to the target basis or to $0$, and have kernels spanned by the killed basis subset. These exact integral and bar-compatible maps, not arbitrary field summands, are used in tensor inheritance.

derivations.claim: **Existence.** Apply [F1] degree by degree, and note that the residue target is the free $\mathbb Z$-span of $\mathcal B$ in each finite root or label component. The lift $G(b)$ of residue $b$ exists in $E_{\mathbb Z}$, is bar invariant by [F1], and the direct sums over degrees give a family $G(\mathcal B)$ with the asserted spanning properties over $A$, $A_0$ and $A_\infty$; adaptedness to the string ideals is the corresponding clause of [F1].

**Uniqueness.** Let $g,h\in M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ have the same residue class in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$. Then $g-h\in E_{\mathbb Z}\cap qL$ lies in the kernel of the canonical map of [F2], which is injective in the balanced case; hence $g=h$. Applied to $g=G(b)$ and an arbitrary lift of $b$, this is exactly the uniqueness used by later consumers, and it identifies the family defined over either chart.
